turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in. Your partner is on the line. You were content for them to join, yes?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, thank you, Doctor. I asked them to telephone, if that is acceptable.
[SEG0003] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Hello. I'm at work, so I'll only come in where I actually heard something.
[SEG0004] person_1 (DOCTOR): Of course. What has brought you in today?
[SEG0005] person_2 (PATIENT): Yesterday, on the train, I had a sudden tightness in my chest. I was shaking, and I was very frightened. I believed I was having a heart attack.
[SEG0006] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. Take me through it, if you would.

[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. I was standing on the Northern line, on the way in to work. The carriage was packed and someone was eating crisps, which is beside the point. It started all at once. The tightness sat across the middle of my chest for about ten minutes, and it eased after I got off at the next stop.
[SEG0008] person_1 (DOCTOR): The shaking, where was that?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): In my hands, and a little through my legs. The fear was, err, quite overwhelming. I do not think I have ever felt like that.
[SEG0010] person_1 (DOCTOR): Was there pain, or only the tight feeling?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the tightness. There was no pain.
[SEG0012] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did it go into your arm, or up to your jaw?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No. It did not spread at all.
[SEG0014] person_1 (DOCTOR): Were you short of breath at the time?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No. I would not say I was short of breath.
[SEG0016] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any sweating, or feeling sick?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I was a little clammy, yes. I did not feel sick, and I was not sick.
[SEG0018] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): They rang me off the platform and could hardly get a sentence out. They said their heart was hammering.
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, that is correct. I ought to have said. My heart was pounding. I rather played it down.

[SEG0020] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mm. Let me say it back. Tightness across the chest for about ten minutes, shaking, real fear, a bit clammy, heart pounding, and it settled once you left the train. Have I got that?

[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, thank you, that is fair. Though I must correct one thing. I said I was not short of breath. In truth I was gasping. I could not get a full breath in the whole time it was going on.
[SEG0022] person_1 (DOCTOR): Thank you, that matters. Was this the first time? Any illnesses, or any operations?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): The first time, yes. No illnesses. I have never had an operation.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any heart disease in the family?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): My father had a heart attack at 58. I think that is why my mind went straight there.
[SEG0026] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you take any medicines, prescribed or ones you have bought?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing at all. I do not take tablets.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Have you ever had a reaction to a medicine?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): No, never. I have taken penicillin, amoxicilin, for a throat infection some years ago, and I was perfectly fine with it.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, and what do you do for work?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): I have never smoked. I work in accounts, in an office.
[SEG0032] person_1 (DOCTOR): How about your bowels and waterworks, and any headaches?
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Bowels and waterworks are entirely normal. I do not get headaches.
[SEG0034] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll examine you now. Your pulse is 78 and regular, blood pressure is 128 over 76, your chest is clear and the heart sounds are normal.

[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am not going to call this a heart attack. It may have been a panic attack, and equally I cannot exclude a cardiac cause on the history alone. We will see what the tracing shows, but those are the two things in my mind.

[SEG0036] person_1 (DOCTOR): I am booking an ECG before you leave today. I would like you to use a slow breath if it starts again, in for four, hold for four, out for four. And I will see you next week to go over the result.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you, Doctor. I shall practise that. You have been very clear.

spec.situation: Young adult after a first episode of sudden chest tightness, shaking and fear on a train; thinks it was a heart attack; no drugs; partner phones in details; doctor orders ECG, teaches breathing.

traps.happens: The doctor asks about drug reactions. Variants (use ONE per encounter): (a) the patient says 'No, never, I have taken penicillin and everything' (no allergy); (b) the patient is unsure ('maybe the antibiotic or the painkiller, nobody told me which'); (c) a real allergy with the reaction described; (d) allergies are never asked.
traps.label_rule: (a) NO allergy entry: negative_findings 'Allergies' absent. (b) allergy with status uncertain, the substance as described, the reaction if said, plus an allergy_uncertain uncertainty. (c) allergy with the reaction. (d) nothing at all. NEVER list a medicine the patient has taken without a reaction as an allergy, and the plan must not prescribe a drug of a recorded allergy's family.

features: denial_then_admission: the patient first denies a symptom, then later describes it. The label records the symptom as present (the later, fuller answer) and does NOT also record the earlier denial as a negative finding.

doctor_thinks_aloud: the doctor lists possible causes or says what they will not conclude yet. Only record a clinical assessment if the doctor actually states a leading or differential impression; 'let's see what the tests say' is not an assessment.
